name: Wuumu-Mpuono
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Guy Kouarata & Koen Bostoen. 2024. Sound change versus lexical change for subgrouping: word-final lenition of Proto-Bantu *ŋg in West-Coastal Bantu. Language Dynamics and Change 14: 1-73. doi:10.1163/22105832-bja10033 (author accepted manuscript, open)
sources.note: Nothing; Wuumu B78 (Kinkole, Odziba; own fieldwork 2022) and Mpuono B84 figure only as doculects in a segmental sound-change/subgrouping study.

sources.citation: Kouarata, Guy, Sara Pacchiarotti & Koen Bostoen. 2023. Nouvelle contribution à l'inventaire et la description des parlers teke (bantou, B70-80). Linguistique et Langues Africaines 9(2): 1-33. doi:10.4000/lla.12921
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 5.2.10 'Wuumu (B78U, B78V)' gives locations/glossonyms and states 'Le seul ouvrage que nous connaissions sur le wuumu parlé en RDC est le travail de Matakumba Kanika (1980)'; Mpuono B84 only mentioned in classification lists (B84X Kindunu, B84Y Fadiaka from Bastin et al. 1999).

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Natalia Chousou-Polydouri & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Untangling the West-Coastal Bantu mess: identification, geography and phylogeny of the Bantu B50-80 languages. Africana Linguistica 25: 155-229. doi:10.2143/AL.25.0.3287234 (open second proofs from biblio.ugent.be; font-shifted text decoded)
sources.note: Nothing. pp.168-169: 'In a recent linguistic atlas of the DRC (Maalu-Bungi et al.), Mpuono is reported among the DRC Bantu languages for which there is no documentation. There are wordlists in Bastin et al. (1999) for two varieties of Mpuono'; pp.173-174: Wuumu known from wordlists and ethnographic surveys; p.~226 lists Wuumu among varieties 'in urgent need of being described'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page and JSON for Wuumu-Mpuono [wuum1239] (Hammarström et al.), incl. Ethnologue comment and Glottolog's most extensive description
sources.note: Nothing; Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist (Makouta-Mboukou 1980, 7 pp; Maes & Boone 1935); 4 refs, none descriptive.

sources.citation: BantuFirst / Ghent University (Kouarata, Pacchiarotti, Bostoen) 2021-2022 field data on Wuumu B78 (Kinkole DRC; Odziba Rep. Congo) and any forthcoming phonological sketch; annexes to Kouarata et al. 2023, LLA 9(2) (650-item tone-marked lexical correspondences)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only modern first-hand data on Wuumu; the team could state whether the variety has (stem-initial) accent as in other Teke languages or is purely tonal. Annexes at journals.openedition.org/lla (doi:10.4000/lla.12921) were not downloaded; they are wordlists, not prose.

sources.citation: Maalu-Bungi, Crispin et al. (Atlas linguistique de la RDC / linguistic atlas of the DRC, cited in Pacchiarotti et al. 2019: 168) — entry for Mpuono
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The survey that lists Mpuono B84 as undocumented; would confirm absence of any description rather than supply a stress statement.

sources.citation: Makouta-Mboukou, Jean-Pierre. 1980. Clés sociolinguistiques de l'écologie fumu et wumu. In Luc Bouquiaux (ed.), L'expansion bantoue: Actes du Colloque International du CNRS, Viviers 4-16 avril 1977, vol. 2, 793-805. Paris: SELAF.

sources.note: Only published item with Wuumu (Rep. Congo) data by a linguist who described neighbouring Fumu; may carry transcription conventions/notes on tone or accent, though Glottolog rates it wordlist-level.

sources.citation: Matakumba Kanika, Mirel. 1980. Structure phonologique et morphologique de la langue teke (B.75). Lubumbashi: Université nationale du Zaïre, Campus de Lubumbashi (mémoire de graduat).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Per Kouarata, Pacchiarotti & Bostoen 2023 the only existing work on Wuumu as spoken in DRC; a 'structure phonologique' chapter is the one place a statement on accent/tone for this languoid could exist. Identity (B.75 label vs B78 Wuumu) must be verified.

sources.citation: Bastin, Yvonne, André Coupez & Michael Mann. 1999. Continuity and divergence in the Bantu languages: perspectives from a lexicostatistic study. Tervuren: MRAC.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Lexicostatistical wordlists only (Mpuono 1 Kindunu, Mpuono 2 Fadiaka; Fumu-Wumbu 3-6), per Kouarata et al. 2023 Annexe; no prosody expected.
